title: August and the Gravity
premise: Felix Crane tends the Verdance, a terraformed garden on a dead moon, growing an atmosphere for colonists who may never come because the two fleets that seeded this system now refuse to speak. When a ghost ship's manifest lists her long-dead brother's name alongside an unfamiliar one, Felix discovers both fleets' truce rests on a fabricated signal she once transmitted to prevent mutual annihilation. As the truce expires and hardliners on both sides move toward war, Felix must keep the lie alive while hunting the truth of who really fired first. In the end she broadcasts the full record to both fleets at once, gambling that the found family she's gathered among defectors from each side can survive a truth that nearly destroyed them.
about_author: Rosalind Fairweather is a former hydrologist who spent six years on remote research stations before turning to fiction, and her work is known for treating ecology as character. She writes from a coastal town where she keeps a stubborn greenhouse of plants that should not survive there.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She runs supply between the two silent fleet stations, tending the Verdance garden alone between runs. Establishes her ritual, her loneliness, and the fragile truce everyone treats as weather. Emotional beat: quiet devotion to a future no one believes in.

chapters.title: A Name on the Manifest
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Docking records show the Meridian—a ship lost with her brother aboard—logged a departure last week, listing his name and a stranger's: Ilsa Vey. Felix breaks protocol to investigate the derelict berth. Emotional beat: grief cracked open by impossible hope.

chapters.title: What the Garden Remembers
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa, a fleet archivist turned deserter, hides in the Verdance and reveals the Meridian was scuttled deliberately—its crew knew something about the war's first shot. She sought out Felix by name. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two people guarding secrets.

chapters.title: The Signal That Held
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Flashback threads reveal Felix once forged a distress transmission that made both fleets believe a third party attacked them, freezing them into truce. Ilsa has found evidence the forgery is unraveling in fleet archives. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing as responsibility.

chapters.title: Hardliners
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A fleet inspection arrives at the Verdance; Commander Ostrander suspects the garden is being used to smuggle messages between fleets. Felix must lie convincingly for the first time in her honest life. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Table
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa brokers a secret meeting between sympathetic officers of both fleets aboard the restored Meridian, using Felix's garden seedlings as neutral cargo. The meeting almost works until someone recognizes the forged signal's signature. Emotional beat: hope built on borrowed time.

chapters.title: Expiration
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The truce formally lapses; both fleets mobilize, and Ostrander arrests Ilsa as a spy. Felix learns the stranger's name on the manifest was bait—Ilsa was sent to find whoever sent the original signal. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as desperate trust.

chapters.title: Who Fired First
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Interrogated, Ilsa shares what the Meridian's logs prove: neither fleet fired first—an automated defense grid did, and both admiralties buried it to preserve their casus belli. Felix realizes her lie accidentally prevented justice but also genocide. Emotional beat: the weight of an unforgivable kindness.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. With hours before the fleets engage over the Verdance itself, Felix and escaped Ilsa hijack the garden's atmospheric relay array and transmit the Meridian's full logs—and Felix's confession—to every ship in the system. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into courage.

chapters.title: Ground Truth
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Weapons stand down as crews absorb the record; both admiralties fracture, but joint salvage crews arrive at the Verdance not as occupiers but as volunteers. The garden will be planted by many hands. Felix finally belongs to the future she grew. Emotional beat: belonging earned through truth.
